title: Reading financial statements
objectives: Read the P&L, balance sheet and cash flow statement.
body_md:
Three statements tell the company story.

## Profit and loss (income statement)

Revenue, less operating costs gives **EBITDA**; less depreciation gives **EBIT**; less interest and tax gives **net profit (PAT)**. **EPS = PAT ÷ shares**.

## Balance sheet

**Assets = Liabilities + Equity.** Current assets (cash, receivables, inventory) fund current liabilities. Non-current assets, borrowings and net worth show structure.

## Cash flow statement

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| Operating (CFO) | Cash generated by the business |
| Investing (CFI) | Capex, investments, asset sales |
| Financing (CFF) | Debt, equity, dividends |

**Free cash flow = CFO − capex.**

## How they link

- PAT flows into retained earnings on the balance sheet.
- Depreciation is deducted in the P&L but added back in cash flow (non-cash).
- Changes in working capital move cash without moving profit.

> **Exam tip:** Profit is an opinion, cash is a fact. Compare PAT with CFO every year.
example: A company shows ₹100 crore PAT but only ₹20 crore CFO because receivables doubled. Profit is booked but cash has not arrived: a warning sign.
say: Profit and cash flow tell different stories; we check both.
Free cash flow is what is left after the business is maintained and grown.
never: Net profit is all that matters.

check.why: FCF = operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

check.q: The accounting identity on the balance sheet is:
check.why: Every asset is funded by liabilities or equity.
